method: Headlines collected via web search (fetch_news.py collector blocked in sandbox; use it for local/Actions runs). Entity sentiment scored by Claude during the weekly Cowork routine. sentiment = 0-100 D-favorability of coverage tone (matches existing dashboard sentimentScore semantics: >55 leans D, <45 leans R). candidateSentiment = 0-100 favorability of coverage toward that candidate personally. outletLean: -2 left ... +2 right (AllSides-style); null = unrated outlet, excluded from scatter.

races.matchup: Susan Collins (R, inc.) vs. Troy Jackson (D)
races.summary: Coverage of the last two weeks centers on Democrat Troy Jackson's narrow polling edge over incumbent Republican Susan Collins. A UNH Survey Center Pine Tree Poll (July 15-20) had Jackson up 49-46, and a Senate Majority PAC poll showed him ahead 49-45, both within the margin of error, keeping the race a toss-up. Jackson launched his first general-election ad touting his labor-organizer background and attacking Collins, and reporting has focused on abortion rights and women voters as potentially decisive, given Collins' 2018 Kavanaugh vote. Jackson became the nominee after initial primary winner Graham Platner withdrew.

races.matchup: Hannah Pingree (D) vs. Bobby Charles (R) vs. Rick Bennett (I) — OPEN seat (Mills term-limited)
races.summary: The Maine Education Association endorsed Democrat Hannah Pingree on Aug 6, reinforcing her position as the heavy favorite in this open race (Mills term-limited). Late-July polling had Pingree leading Bobby Charles ~49-35 with independent Rick Bennett in single digits, and she dominates fundraising (~$850K cash on hand). Pingree and Bennett agreed to four televised debates.

races.summary: Progressive Abdul El-Sayed narrowly won the Aug. 4 Democratic primary over Rep. Haley Stevens (by about 1 point), and coverage has emphasized his challenge in uniting a fractured party; he said he spoke with Barack Obama about campaigning together. Republican Mike Rogers, unopposed for his nomination, moved immediately to court disaffected moderate Democrats with a direct video appeal, and pre-primary polling showed Rogers leading El-Sayed by roughly 3-10 points. Both went sharply negative. The seat (retiring Sen. Gary Peters) is rated a national toss-up.

John James won the GOP side with roughly 50% over Perry Johnson. Benson holds a polling edge (a feed average of about +7.6, with individual reads from +2 to +13) and a large money advantage, ending with over $6.4M cash on hand versus James' $1.4M. The two drew early battle lines immediately. Cook Political Report rates the open seat lean Democratic.

races.matchup: Jon Husted (R, inc.) vs. Sherrod Brown (D)
races.summary: This appointed-incumbent race is rated a toss-up, with most public polling showing Brown narrowly ahead and affordability/health-care costs dominating the debate. Brown comfortably outraised Husted again in Q2 as outside groups entered the race, and at the Ohio Democratic Party dinner on 8/2 party leaders struck their most optimistic tone in years. Both candidates say they'd like to debate but none is yet scheduled; AFP canvassing warns as many as one in five reliable GOP voters are wavering.

The Cook Political Report shifted the race from 'Lean Republican' to 'Toss Up,' citing Ramaswamy's likability problems, with 270toWin's average showing Acton narrowly ahead (~48% to 46.7%). Acton has outraised the self-funding billionaire for multiple straight quarters (nearly $22M cumulative) though Ramaswamy retains a large cash edge from a $25M personal loan. Recent coverage centered on dueling data-center/energy plans and Acton breaking with Ohio Democrats to back the Issue 3 voter-ID amendment.

races.matchup: Jon Ossoff (D, inc.) vs. Mike Collins (R)
races.summary: Ossoff leads consistently (52% in a late-July AARP/bipartisan poll; 56%-43% in a June Fox News poll) and holds a commanding fundraising edge — $81M raised, $42M cash on hand vs. Collins' ~$2.2M. Coverage has been rough for Collins, who faced sustained scrutiny over his son-in-law's antisemitic/white-nationalist social posts and is highlighting Black-conservative support in response. Ossoff picked up a cross-party endorsement from former GOP Sen. Jeff Flake on 8/5, and Atlanta debates are now set for Oct. 8 and Oct. 13.

races.matchup: Rick Jackson (R) vs. Keisha Lance Bottoms (D)
races.summary: Open seat (Kemp term-limited). The race is effectively deadlocked — Bottoms and Jackson sit within the margin of error in the late-July AARP poll, even as the broader environment tilts D. Jackson, a self-funding billionaire healthcare executive who upset Trump/Kemp-backed Burt Jones in the runoff, launched an $87M ad buy and re-secured Trump's endorsement. Bottoms went up with her first attack ad on 8/5 tying Jackson to Trump, and the two clashed over data centers and Medicaid expansion at an 8/5 business luncheon.

races.summary: An AARP-commissioned poll (fielded Jul 26-28, released Aug 6) showed Hobbs leading Biggs 52%-44%. Coverage was dominated by Hobbs' decision (announced ~Jul 30-31) to decline debating Biggs and instead tour the state, which drew both Democratic-favorable poll framing and critical 'dodging debates' coverage. Both campaigns launched attack ads; Biggs picked former state Sen. Sine Kerr as his LG, and the NYT reported Hobbs is eyeing ex-Mesa Mayor John Giles as a running mate.

races.matchup: Pete Ricketts (R, inc.) vs. Dan Osborn (I)
races.summary: In late July-early August 2026, coverage centered on the race tightening into a genuine toss-up: multiple polls show independent Dan Osborn statistically tied with or narrowly leading GOP incumbent Pete Ricketts. Ricketts outraised Osborn ($6.3M, though $5.2M self-funded) in the latest quarter, and both campaigns agreed to a single Sept. 1 debate at the Nebraska State Fair in Grand Island. Conservative outlets pushed a counter-narrative framing Osborn as a Democrat-bankrolled 'fake independent.' Osborn maintains he will not caucus with either party.

Talarico posts large margins with independents, moderates, Black and Latino voters. Paxton countered at an Aug. 6 Houston rally by touting a four-part economic/affordability plan and acknowledging Talarico's ~$30M fundraising head start.

races.matchup: Greg Abbott (R, inc.) vs. Gina Hinojosa (D)
races.summary: Over the last two weeks the race narrative was 'tightening': polls (Fox News 50-49, Texas A&M Bush School/ReconMR 46-45) show Abbott's lead shrinking to within the margin of error and his job approval turning net-negative after 12 years in office. Hinojosa held an Aug. 6 Houston rally tied to the Voting Rights Act anniversary calling the contest 'the most important race in America' and rolled out a populist affordability/education message plus a six-figure cable ad buy. Abbott campaigned near El Paso promoting his 'Keep Texas Affordable' proposals and retains a large fundraising edge (~$25M vs ~$6M). Inside Elections moved the race Solid R -> Likely R on Aug 6.
